subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the native PowerShell smoke lane include both `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or start with a smaller proven command set?
rationale: The direction fits test-infrastructure priorities, but the active PR changes recurring Windows runner scope and current CI shows the full requested command set does not pass.

options.title: Prove Full Command Set
options.body: Keep both requested commands in scope, but land only after the Windows `pwsh` lane passes and the PR includes redacted successful proof.

options.title: Start Narrower
options.body: Land native PowerShell coverage for commands that already pass, then track `build:strict-smoke` as a separate Windows hardening task.

options.title: Defer CI Scope
options.body: Keep the issue open until runner budget and command ownership are settled.

recommendation.title: Prove Full Command Set
recommendation.body: Keep both requested commands in scope, but land only after the Windows `pwsh` lane passes and the PR includes redacted successful proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent overlap across CI stabilization and PowerShell-safe docs tooling.
